clues.text: Paul found this disciple at Lystra, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
Because the local Jews knew his father was Greek, Paul circumcised him before taking him along.
Paul praised the sincere faith that first lived in this man's grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice.
Paul told this young leader not to let anyone look down on his youth, but to set an example for believers.
Paul opened a letter by greeting this man as his true child in the faith.
Writing to the Thessalonians, Paul said this man had just come back with good news of their faith and love.
Paul told the Philippians he had nobody else like this man who would truly care for their needs.
